## Document authority

This document defines required infrastructure capabilities and records the
status of implementation options. It does not certify that a named service is
available, approved, compliant, or correctly configured. Only an explicit
decision by the authorized WBG and project owners changes a candidate service
to `Approved`.
:::

# Purpose

The AI-assisted harmonization system needs a controlled environment in which it
can register survey sources, structure documentation, draft and review
specifications, execute approved logic, validate outputs, and preserve a full
audit trail.

This document consolidates the earlier ITS requirements note, concise request,
and round-one question list. It separates durable capabilities from provisional
Azure product mappings so that an unapproved proposal cannot become architecture
by repetition.

# Status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Required | Capability is necessary to satisfy the canonical architecture |
| Proposed | Preferred option or design awaiting accountable approval |
| Under review | Submitted to the relevant owner; response pending |
| Approved | Explicitly accepted for a defined scope and configuration |
| Rejected | Considered and not accepted, with rationale |
| Open | Requirement or decision is not sufficiently defined |

Product names in this document are `Proposed` unless a decision record states
otherwise.

# Capability requirements

## Source and artifact storage

The system requires durable storage for source files, structured extracts,
specifications, logs, and outputs. It must support:

- data classification and access separation by artifact class;
- immutable identity through hashes and versioning;
- prevention or detection of source overwrite;
- encryption and institutionally approved key management;
- private or otherwise approved network access;
- backup, recovery, retention, legal hold, and deletion policies;
- access logging suitable for restricted survey data; and
- controlled access from compute, review, and audit services.

Raw sources, mutable workflow state, and published outputs must not be conflated
merely because one object store can hold all three.

## Structured sources of truth

The system needs transactional storage for canonical schema metadata, workflow
state, approvals, run manifests, and related structured records. Requirements
include:

- schema constraints and referential integrity;
- concurrency control and idempotent state transitions;
- version history and auditable changes;
- role-based read and write permissions; and
- backup, restore, retention, and availability appropriate to each record type.

The canonical GMD schema and historical precedents are logically separate even
if an implementation shares infrastructure. Rules are authoritative; precedents
are advisory.

## Enterprise model inference

The system requires an institutionally approved model endpoint for
documentation extraction, drafting, and bounded diagnosis. Approval must define:

- permitted data classifications and fields;
- tenant, region, residency, retention, abuse-monitoring, and training-use terms;
- private endpoint or approved network path;
- identity and authorization model;
- model and deployment version control;
- quotas, rate limits, capacity, and cost controls;
- prompt and response logging policy; and
- an incident and service-degradation path.

No raw respondent-level microdata may be sent to a model under the default
architecture. Approval of a platform does not itself approve every payload.

## Historical retrieval

The system needs hybrid retrieval over quality-assured precedents and selected
documentation. It must support:

- structured filtering by survey, country, wave, module, variable, status, and
  schema version;
- keyword and, where justified, semantic similarity retrieval;
- citations back to the complete source, approval, and QA lineage;
- index and embedding versioning;
- withdrawal or suppression of superseded precedents;
- evaluation of retrieval relevance and access leakage; and
- authorization filtering before retrieval results reach a model or user.

A dedicated "vector database" is an implementation option, not a logical
requirement. The requirement is governed, attributable retrieval.

## Compute and orchestration

The system needs isolated execution for event-driven and batch workloads:

- deterministic profiling and document processing;
- model-assisted drafting;
- bounded, non-production sandbox runs;
- production execution of approved specifications only;
- quality assurance and publication tasks; and
- scheduled precedent-index maintenance.

The platform must provide workload identity, resource quotas, timeouts,
concurrency limits, retry policy, idempotency, deployment versioning, and direct
operational visibility for the authorized team. Compute selection must follow
measured workload and control requirements; a container platform does not by
itself guarantee low idle cost or scale-to-zero behavior.

## Sandbox isolation

The pre-approval sandbox is a separate trust zone. It requires:

- separation from production authorization and credentials;
- access only to an approved survey copy or scope;
- bounded CPU, memory, time, iteration count, and cost;
- restricted outbound connectivity;
- an allowlist of executable operations and dependencies;
- complete iteration and diagnostic logging; and
- a field-level policy for diagnostics returned to the model.

Sandbox success never creates production approval.

## Human review and workflow control

Review requires an authenticated interface that lets an authorized expert:

- inspect source evidence, rules, precedents, uncertainty, and proposed logic;
- approve, reject, or amend decisions with reasons;
- see and compare versions;
- sign an exact specification hash;
- manage conflicts and stale reviews; and
- submit decisions through validated state transitions.

Immutable artifact storage is not sufficient as the workflow control plane.
The implementation must handle concurrent reviews, locking or optimistic
concurrency, duplicate events, idempotency, notification, and authorization.

## Identity, secrets, and network

The preferred control model is identity-based and least-privilege. The approved
design must specify:

- workload and human identities;
- role definitions and segregation of duties;
- managed identity or the approved equivalent;
- secret storage, rotation, expiration, and audit;
- private endpoints, firewall rules, DNS, and egress controls;
- access paths for the Microdata Library and approved package sources; and
- emergency access and revocation procedures.

Long-lived credentials embedded in source code, images, prompts, or files are
prohibited.

## Observability and audit

The system needs operational telemetry and a separate, durable audit record.
Together they must cover:

- correlation across intake, draft, review, execution, QA, and publication;
- actor or workload identity and timestamps;
- source, specification, schema, engine, model, and QA versions;
- output hashes and disposition;
- model call metadata consistent with data policy;
- failed authorization and data-access events;
- alerting, dashboards, and team read access; and
- retention, tamper evidence, export, and investigation procedures.

Application logs alone are not the approval ledger or execution manifest.

## Delivery and software supply chain

Implementation repositories require an approved delivery path with:

- version control and protected branches;
- automated tests and policy checks;
- artifact and container registry;
- dependency locking, vulnerability scanning, and provenance;
- environment-specific deployment approvals;
- rollback and withdrawal procedures; and
- separation between development, sandbox, and production identities.

## Notification

Reviewers and operators need approved notifications for drafts, rejected or
stale reviews, failed runs, QA disposition, and incidents. Notifications should
contain identifiers and links, not restricted data or model payloads.

# Environment model

At minimum, the system needs the following separation:

| Environment | Purpose | Data | Production authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Development | Contract, code, and UI development | Synthetic or approved non-production data | None |
| Sandbox | Bounded pre-approval execution and diagnosis | Approved limited survey scope | None |
| Production | Authorized deterministic runs and QA | Approved operational data | Exact approved specifications only |

Separation may use subscriptions, clusters, namespaces, accounts, or another
approved mechanism, but identities, permissions, secrets, and audit records must
make the boundary enforceable.

# Data and model decision matrix

| Payload | Default model status | Decision needed |
|---|---|---|
| Public or approved survey documentation | Open | Classification, endpoint, retention, logging |
| Restricted questionnaires or codebooks | Open | Data-owner and platform approval |
| DDI or extracted metadata | Open | Field classification and provenance policy |
| Aggregated variable profile | Open | Allowed statistics, thresholds, suppression |
| Row-level microdata | Prohibited | Architecture exception plus data-owner and security approval |
| Sandbox diagnostics | Open | Allowlisted fields, redaction, retention |
| Approved precedents | Open | Authorization filtering and model-use approval |
| Prompts and model responses | Open | Storage, access, retention, incident handling |

# Candidate service mapping

The following mappings preserve what earlier drafts proposed without treating
the proposals as approved facts.

| Capability | Candidate options from archived drafts | Status | Required decision evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Object storage | Azure Blob Storage or ADLS Gen2 | Under review | Data classification, network, identity, retention, immutability |
| Relational records | Azure SQL Database or PostgreSQL on Azure | Under review | Approved standard, ownership, availability, backup, access |
| Model endpoint | Azure OpenAI Service or approved Azure AI/Foundry deployment | Under review | Tenant availability, region, payload policy, retention, quota |
| Hybrid retrieval | Azure AI Search with vector capability or approved alternative | Under review | Access filtering, lineage, index lifecycle, evaluation |
| Batch compute | AKS as an earlier target; simpler managed container or job service for PoC | Under review | Workload fit, isolation, access, operations, cost, migration |
| Monitoring | Azure Monitor and Log Analytics or institutional standard | Under review | Onboarding, retention, audit separation, team access |
| Review interface | Posit Connect application or Azure-hosted web application | Under review | Identity, hosting, storage access, workflow semantics, support |
| Notification | Approved email, Teams, or event-driven service | Open | Trigger, content, authorization, support model |

No service-specific security, residency, training-use, or cost claim is accepted
without current documentation for the exact tenant, region, configuration, and
contractual terms.

# Responsibility model

| ITS or platform authority | GMD project team | Joint decision |
|---|---|---|
| Approve and provision institutional platforms | Define methodology, contracts, prompts, and pipeline behavior | Data classification and model payload policy |
| Configure baseline network, identity, security, backup, and monitoring controls | Build, test, deploy, and support project applications within granted access | Environment and segregation design |
| Publish service constraints and operational support model | Review and approve harmonization specifications | Production access and release controls |
| Maintain underlying managed services as agreed | Curate rules, precedents, QA policy, and project audit evidence | Incident response and retention |

The exact responsibility assignment must be agreed service by service. Earlier
drafts assumed broad ITS and GMD roles but did not establish an approved RACI.

# Questions requiring authoritative answers

The detailed round-one questionnaire remains in the archive. The canonical
questions are:

1. Which storage service and configuration are approved for each survey data
   classification, and what immutability, retention, backup, and access logging
   controls are mandatory?
2. Can approved compute access the Microdata Library and package sources, and
   through what egress or allowlist process?
3. Which relational and workflow-state platforms are standard and available?
4. Which enterprise model endpoints are approved, in which regions, and for
   exactly which documentation, metadata, profile, diagnostic, and precedent
   fields?
5. What are the model endpoint's retention, monitoring, quota, and capacity
   constraints for the approved configuration?
6. Which retrieval service supports authorization-aware keyword and similarity
   search with attributable results?
7. Which compute platform best fits development, bounded sandbox, and production
   batch workloads, and what self-service deployment and log access can the team
   receive?
8. How will workload identity, secret management, private connectivity, and
   environment separation be implemented?
9. What are the approved monitoring and audit services, retention periods, and
   direct query rights for the project team?
10. Where can the review application be hosted, how will users authenticate, and
    which workflow-state service will prevent stale or duplicate approvals?
11. Which notification mechanism is approved for review and operational events?
12. Which CI/CD, registry, dependency, vulnerability, and release controls are
    mandatory?
13. Who owns service operation, application support, incident response, cost,
    and approvals at each lifecycle stage?
14. What is the smallest approved proof-of-concept configuration that does not
    preclude a secure production design?

# Decision gates

## Before a proof of concept with institutional data

- Data owner approves the survey sources and field-level model payload policy.
- ITS or the platform authority approves the selected services and regions.
- Development and sandbox isolation, identity, secrets, logging, and cost limits
  are tested.
- The specification, approval, execution, and QA contracts are versioned.
- A human reviewer and incident owner are named.

## Before production

- The architecture threat model and privacy review are accepted.
- Production authorization verifies exact approval and content hashes.
- Backup, recovery, retention, withdrawal, and incident procedures are tested.
- Retrieval and model behavior are evaluated on held-out surveys.
- Monitoring, audit export, support, capacity, and cost controls are operational.
- Repository and service ownership is documented.
